name: Token Rank Probability
description: Analyzes the statistical rank of words within a model's vocabulary distribution. AI language models operate by predicting the most statistically probable next word (token) in a sequence. As a result, AI-generated text over-indexes on 'Top 10' or 'Top 100' high-probability words for any given context. Human writers naturally draw from a much wider, less predictable vocabulary distribution, frequently selecting 'long-tail' words that a machine would score as low-probability.
mechanism: The method processes the text through a reference language model to calculate the absolute ranking of every word based on its preceding context. Words are categorized into probability tiers (e.g., Top 10, Top 100, Top 1000, >1000). The algorithm calculates the aggregate fraction of high-rank vs. low-rank tokens. AI text exhibits an artificially smooth, dense concentration of Top 10/100 words (the 'Green/Yellow' zones in GLTR visualizations). Human text is characterized by sudden spikes of low-probability, highly specific words (the 'Red/Purple' zones) that break the algorithmic sequence.
useCase: Highly effective for analyzing formal essays, news articles, and professional writing. It provides deep mathematical proof of generative origins by exposing the underlying predictive mechanism of the text.
strengths:
• Rooted in the core architecture of how all autoregressive language models mathematically operate.
• Extremely resilient against simple synonym-swapping, as the underlying probability distribution remains artificially smooth.
limitations:
• Requires significant computational resources, as the text must be evaluated against a heavyweight reference language model.
• Short texts (under 100 words) do not provide a large enough statistical sample to calculate reliable rank variations.
parameters:
Analysis: Autoregressive Token Prediction and Absolute Rank Categorization
Metric: Distribution Density across Probability Tiers (Top 10/100/1000)
Output: 0-100 Algorithmic Rank Predictability Score
accuracy: High — 85-90% accuracy. This is one of the most reliable, mathematically grounded methods for detecting raw, unedited AI text.

references.title: Gehrmann, S. et al. (2019). GLTR: Statistical Detection and Visualization of Generated Text. ACL Demo.
Solaiman, I. et al. (2019). Release Strategies and the Social Impacts of Language Models. arXiv.
